title: A budget model that holds up
goal: You will build a clean three-year revenue and operating profit model controlled by a Base/Upside scenario toggle.

steps.action: Enter the assumptions block labels and headers in cells A1:D8.
steps.where: Worksheet grid, starting at cell A1 below the ribbon.
steps.why: A dedicated assumptions block keeps model inputs organized and auditable.
steps.checkpoint: You should see "Assumptions" in A1, "Scenario" in A2, and Driver, Base, Upside, and Active across A4:D4, with four driver names in A5:A8.
hint_levels: Build the input section in the upper-left corner.
Use A5:A8 for Starting Revenue, Growth, Gross Margin, and Annual OpEx.
Enter A1 Assumptions; A2 Scenario; A4 Driver; B4 Base; C4 Upside; D4 Active; then enter the four driver names in A5:A8.

steps.action: Enter the Base and Upside assumption values in B5:C8.
steps.where: Worksheet grid, inside the assumptions block under the Base and Upside headers.
steps.why: Two assumption sets provide the inputs that the scenario toggle will switch between.
steps.checkpoint: You should see 100000 in B5:C5, 10% and 20% in B6:C6, 60% and 65% in B7:C7, and 40000 and 45000 in B8:C8.
hint_levels: Fill both scenario columns with a complete set of drivers.
Starting Revenue is unchanged; Growth, Gross Margin, and Annual OpEx differ by scenario.

steps.action: Create a Base/Upside dropdown in cell B2.
steps.where: Data tab > Data Tools group > Data Validation dialog.
steps.why: A validated dropdown makes scenario changes fast and prevents invalid entries.
steps.checkpoint: Cell B2 should display Base and show a dropdown arrow when selected, with Base and Upside as its choices.
hint_levels: Use Excel's input-validation feature on the scenario cell.
Set B2 to allow a List whose source contains the two scenario names.
Select B2, choose Data > Data Validation > Data Validation, set Allow to List, enter Base,Upside in Source, click OK, and select Base.

steps.action: Enter an XLOOKUP formula in D5 and fill it down through D8.
steps.where: Formula bar for cell D5, then the fill handle at the lower-right corner of the selected cell.
steps.why: The Active column converts the selected scenario into one consistent set of model drivers.
steps.checkpoint: With Base selected in B2, D5:D8 should display 100000, 10%, 60%, and 40000.
hint_levels: Match the scenario name to the headers above the two input columns.
Look up $B$2 in $B$4:$C$4 and return the corresponding value from each row.
In D5 enter =XLOOKUP($B$2,$B$4:$C$4,B5:C5), press Enter, then drag D5's fill handle down to D8.

steps.action: Enter the output table labels and year headers in A11:D15.
steps.where: Worksheet grid, starting at cell A11 beneath the assumptions block.
steps.why: A compact output section separates calculated results from editable drivers.
steps.checkpoint: You should see "Model Outputs" in A11, years 2026–2028 in B12:D12, and Revenue, Gross Profit, Annual OpEx, and Operating Profit in A13:A16.
hint_levels: Place the reporting section a few rows below the assumptions.
Use one header row for three years and one row for each financial metric.
Enter A11 Model Outputs; B12:D12 2026, 2027, 2028; and A13:A16 Revenue, Gross Profit, Annual OpEx, Operating Profit.

steps.action: Build the three-year revenue calculation across B13:D13.
steps.where: Formula bar and worksheet cells B13:D13 in the Model Outputs section.
steps.why: Revenue establishes the model's time-based calculation chain.
steps.checkpoint: Under Base, the Revenue row should show 100000, 110000, and 121000 before currency formatting.
hint_levels: Start with Active Starting Revenue, then grow each later year from the previous year.
B13 should link to D5, while C13 and D13 should multiply the prior year by one plus D6.
Enter =$D$5 in B13, enter =B13*(1+$D$6) in C13, then drag C13's fill handle across to D13.

steps.action: Enter the Gross Profit, Annual OpEx, and Operating Profit formulas and fill them across all three years.
steps.where: Formula bar for cells B14:B16, then the fill handle across columns C:D.
steps.why: These formulas turn the active assumptions into the model's key profitability outputs.
steps.checkpoint: Under Base, Operating Profit should display 20000, 26000, and 32600 before currency formatting.
hint_levels: Calculate profit from revenue and margin, link OpEx to its active driver, then subtract.
Use Revenue × Active Gross Margin for row 14, Active Annual OpEx for row 15, and Gross Profit − Annual OpEx for row 16.
Enter =B13*$D$7 in B14, =$D$8 in B15, and =B14-B15 in B16; select B14:B16 and drag the fill handle across to D16.

steps.action: Apply distinct input, header, percentage, and currency formatting to the assumptions and output blocks.
steps.where: Home tab > Font, Alignment, Number, and Styles groups.
steps.why: Consistent visual conventions make inputs, calculations, and outputs easy to scan.
steps.checkpoint: The section titles and table headers should stand out, B5:C8 should have an input fill color, percentages should show as percentages, and financial values should show currency with no decimals.
hint_levels: Use color and number formats to distinguish editable cells from results.
Format A1:D1 and A11:D11 as section titles, A4:D4 and A12:D12 as headers, B6:D7 as percentages, and financial cells as currency.

Use Home > Cell Styles or Font for titles and headers; apply a light fill to B5:C8; select B6:D7 and choose Percent Style; select B5:D5, B8:D8, and B13:D16 and choose Currency with zero decimal places.

steps.action: Switch the scenario dropdown to Upside and confirm that the active assumptions and outputs recalculate.
steps.where: Dropdown arrow in cell B2 within the assumptions block.
steps.why: Testing the toggle verifies that the model responds correctly without changing formulas.
steps.checkpoint: B2 should show Upside, D6:D8 should show 20%, 65%, and $45,000, and Operating Profit should show $20,000, $33,000, and $48,600 across 2026–2028.
hint_levels: Use the control at the top of the assumptions block and watch both sections.
Changing B2 to Upside should update D5:D8 first and then recalculate the output table.
Select B2, click its dropdown arrow, choose Upside, and verify D6:D8 plus B16:D16 against the checkpoint values.
